thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — GPU queue growth detected for pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3. queue_length=12480, throttled_requests=3.2k, autoscaler_status=FAILED (scale_limit_reached). Investigate.

pagerduty: @Ciara on-call (sre) — paging now.

Ciara: ack I'm awake, looking. tagging Alex for infra-side metrics.

Alex: diving in. initial glance: autoscaler attempted +6 instances but hit tenant-scale cap. HPA/allocator logs show repeated placement failures: "no compatible MIG slice" and a lot of small free slices across nodes.

Jenna: support — seeing a spike of 503s from a handful of enterprise customers in eu-west. Not full region, but two high-QPS customers.

Mohit: can we confirm MIG sizes? my hypothesis: recent batch jobs used heterogeneous MIG configs and binpack left many unallocatable fragments.

Alex: correct. current node inventory: 8 nodes with 1xMIG-1g, 4 nodes with 2xMIG-2g, remainder mixed. New requests need 3g-equivalent and allocator can't join slices. result: autoscaler created pods but scheduler couldn't place -> backpressure -> queue growth.

Ciara: immediate mitigation options?

Alex: short list: 1) enable emergency temporary burstpool to accept low-priority requests (fast) 2) force-repack nodes via drain/evict to consolidate MIGs (risky, longer) 3) increase tenant-scale cap (won't help if fragmentation prevents placement) 4) route traffic to another region (customer-visible, last resort).

Jenna: customers flagged for impact: corp-x (kt-prod), shopify-integrations (kt-prod). Support notified both with "degraded" status, ETA unknown.

Ciara: let's do 1 + 2 in parallel. Alex, flip burstpool for eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 (low-prio queue) and start a controlled repack of 2 nodes first. I'll coordinate with Mohit for safe eviction windows.

Alex: running command to enable burstpool (ops-bot will log):
```
./infractl pools patch eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 --burstpool-enabled=true --burstpool-cap=0.15
```
ops-bot: burstpool toggle logged by ops-bot (runbook ref #repack-3).

Alex: starting repack on node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-18 — draining low-pri pods first. Commands: `kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

Mohit: monitoring scheduler events + allocation failures. I'll attach a live grep of allocator errors.

Alex: allocator error excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z ERROR allocator placement failed: requested={{gpus:3}} available_fragments=[{node:node-gpu-12, slices:[1,1]},{node:node-gpu-14, slices:[2]}] reason="no single fragment meets request"
```

Ciara: good evidence for fragmentation. Jenna, please update impacted customers: "We’ve enabled temporary burst capacity and are repacking a small set of nodes to recover placements — some requests may see reduced throughput while we work; will follow up in 30m."

Jenna: message sent to corp-x and shopify-integrations support contacts. Both acknowledged.

Support: corp-x asked for an SLA credit check; forwarded to finance/sre-ops.

Mohit: queue length trending down to ~7.2k after burstpool flip, throttled_requests dropping. Repack progress: node-gpu-17 drained, evac completed; MIG slices consolidated on node-gpu-16. Starting kubelet restart for slice reclamation on node-gpu-18.

Ciara: any risk of losing long-running jobs? monitor eviction counts. prioritize not evicting customer-prod jobs.

Alex: we only evicted low-priority batch workers, 0 prod evictions. running `nvidia-smi --mig` confirms the new slice layout is more allocable.

Mohit: autoscaler trial: triggered +2 instances, both placed successfully. scheduler accepts new pods.

ops-bot: autoscaler event: scale up succeeded +2 instances at 02:34Z.

Jenna: customers report reduced errors, corp-x says latency still a bit higher but stable.

Ciara: plan for next 2 hours: continue incremental repack to reduce fragmentation, maintain burstpool at 15% for low-priority soak, monitor autoscaler for any further scale_limit hits. If we see scale_limit again, we consider temporary tenant-scale increase with product approval.

Alex: creating a short-lived orchestration job to reconfigure MIG sizes on 3 candidate hosts overnight (low traffic window). Will post the exact nodes and ETA in this thread.

Mohit: adding watch scripts to alert if queue growth rate exceeds 100 reqs/s for >5m.

Support: raising a ticket for each impacted customer with notes and remediation steps.

Ciara: status update in 45m unless anything regresses. big thanks to team. :thumbsup:

Alex: follow-up — repack of 6 nodes completed, overall fragmentation metric decreased from 0.68 -> 0.12 (allocator metric). queue_length now 382, throttled_requests 0.

Mohit: autoscaler healthy and able to provision matching MIG configs now. No further placement failures observed in logs.

Jenna: sent final update to affected customers; corp-x closing incident on their side.

Ciara: marking incident as mitigated. creating postmortem ticket and assigning to Alex + Mohit for root cause & remediation (owner: Alex). Action items: 1) automated repack schedule during low-traffic windows 2) improve allocator heuristics to allow cross-slice coalescing 3) add a safety lane for emergency tenant-scale expansion.

ops-bot: incident closed (mitigated) by Ciara at 02:58Z — follow-up PR and postmortem required.

Ciara: good work everyone. logging postmortem draft with timeline and metrics.

Alex: will add the allocator error traces and MIG layout before/after to the postmortem.

Mohit: will propose a safe default for burstpool caps to prevent customer-visible routing next time.

Jenna: will coordinate customer-facing postmortem summary.

Support: thumbs up. :white_check_mark:
